refs: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 42 (Management of pediatric trauma)

steps.say: Blunt force causes nearly all childhood injury, and the brain decides survival. Blunt injury causes over 90 percent of paediatric trauma, traumatic brain injury leads death and disability with 60000 admissions yearly, and children under 4 with hypotension, low Glasgow score, coagulopathy or hypoglycemia fare worst.
steps.tx: **Blunt trauma** (non penetrating force) causes over **90** percent of paediatric trauma, **traumatic brain injury** (head damage) leads death and disability with **60000** admissions yearly, and children under **4** with hypotension, low **Glasgow Coma Scale** (consciousness score), coagulopathy or hypoglycemia fare worst.

steps.say: Head injury grades are reported in numbers that every team member understands at once. Head injury grades mild 13 to 15, moderate 9 to 12 and severe 3 to 8 to communicate severity, while nonaccidental trauma stays on every differential with frenulum tears, subconjunctival bleeding, odd bruises, big head and rib fracture under 3 years carrying 95 percent predictive value.
steps.tx: Head injury grades mild **13** to **15**, moderate **9** to **12** and severe **3** to **8** to communicate severity, while **nonaccidental trauma** (inflicted injury) with **child abuse** (harm by carer) stays on every differential, with frenulum tears, subconjunctival bleeding, odd bruises, big head and **rib fracture** under **3** years carrying **95** percent predictive value.

steps.say: Small children run out of oxygen in seconds, so the airway comes before everything else. Children desaturate in seconds from high metabolism and low reserve with hypoxia as the top arrest cause, and a speaking or crying child proves airway patency. A nasogastric tube is banned with basilar skull or midface fracture in favour of an orogastric tube.
steps.tx: Children show rapid **desaturation** (oxygen falling) in seconds from high metabolism and low reserve with hypoxia as the top arrest cause, and a speaking or crying child proves **airway patency** (open breathing passage). A nasogastric tube is banned with basilar skull or midface fracture in favour of an **orogastric tube** (mouth placed).

vis.alt: Supine trauma patient receiving secured airway, cervical collar, chest decompression and haemorrhage control on a board.
vis.caption: Speaking proves a patent airway; secure it early since children desaturate in seconds. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Blood is replacing blood early, because crystalloid alone is drowning small lungs. Resuscitation gives a 20 millilitre per kilogram crystalloid fluid bolus then early O negative blood with massive transfusion thinking, and damage control limits crystalloid. Balanced transfusion and low titre whole blood gain favour, and tranexamic acid loads 15 milligrams per kilogram to 1 gram max then 2 milligrams per kilogram per hour for 8 hours within 3 hours of injury.
steps.tx: Resuscitation gives a **20** mL per kg crystalloid **fluid bolus** (rapid fill) then early O negative blood with **massive transfusion** (blood first strategy) thinking, and damage control limits crystalloid. Balanced transfusion and low titre whole blood gain favour, and **tranexamic acid** (clot stabiliser) loads **15** mg per kg to **1** g max then **2** mg per kg per hour for **8** hours within **3** hours of injury.

steps.say: Doses are worked out per kilogram in advance, because maths fails during a resuscitation. Transfusion doses are packed red blood cells 10 to 20 millilitres per kilogram, plasma 20 millilitres per kilogram, cryoprecipitate 1 unit per 10 kilograms and platelets 15 millilitres per kilogram. Intraosseous access goes in first in the crashing child avoiding injured limbs.
steps.tx: Transfusion doses are **packed red blood cells** (oxygen carriers) **10** to **20** mL per kg, plasma **20** mL per kg, **cryoprecipitate** (clotting concentrate) **1** unit per **10** kg and platelets **15** mL per kg, with **intraosseous access** (bone needle) first in the crashing child avoiding injured limbs.

steps.say: Scan only what changes management, because radiation accumulates across a long childhood. ALARA governs imaging since scanning irradiates growing tissue with dose related brain cancer risk. Routine pan scan and stable patient FAST are out, chest computed tomography is selective with thymus mimicking a wide mediastinum, and FAST keeps a role in unstable pericardial and abdominal bleeding.
steps.tx: **ALARA** (lowest dose imaging) governs scanning since irradiating growing tissue carries dose related brain cancer **radiation risk** (later tumour danger). Routine pan scan and stable patient **FAST** (bedside ultrasound) are out, chest computed tomography stays selective, and FAST keeps a role in unstable pericardial and abdominal bleeding.

steps.say: Grades on scans never dictate care, because the child condition overrules the pictures. Liver and spleen lead solid organ injury and grade never dictates care: stable children observe with brief rest and serial haemoglobin, angioembolization is selective by hemodynamics not blush, routine reimaging is out, instability operates, and splenectomy demands encapsulated vaccines plus age based antibiotic prophylaxis against OPSI.
steps.tx: Liver and spleen lead solid organ injury and grade never dictates care: stable children observe with brief rest and serial haemoglobin (**nonoperative management**), angioembolization is selective by hemodynamics not blush, instability operates, and **splenectomy** (spleen removal) demands encapsulated vaccines plus age based antibiotic prophylaxis against **OPSI** (overwhelming post splenectomy infection).

vis.alt: Spleen diagram showing subcapsular haematoma, parenchymal laceration and haemoperitoneum beside a schematic abdominal CT panel.
vis.caption: Stable spleen and liver injuries observe regardless of grade; splenectomy needs vaccines and prophylaxis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A handlebar to the belly is classically crushing the pancreas against the spine or bursting the duodenum. Handlebar blows classically injure pancreas and duodenum: low grade pancreatic injury without duct damage observes, while distal duct injury gets spleen preserving laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy within 48 hours. Duodenal haematoma resolves in 1 to 3 weeks on tube drainage, bowel rest and parenteral nutrition, and perforation operates.
steps.tx: **Handlebar injury** (bar end to belly) classically causes **pancreatic injury** (gland bruise or duct cut) and **duodenal haematoma** (wall blood clot): low grade injury without duct damage observes, distal duct injury gets spleen preserving laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy within **48** hours, and haematoma resolves in **1** to **3** weeks on tube drainage, bowel rest and parenteral nutrition, while perforation operates.
